{{Short description|Polyhedron with 92 faces}}
{{No footnotes|date=August 2025}}
{{Uniform polyhedra db|Uniform polyhedron stat table|Gisid}}
[[File:Great inverted snub icosidodecahedron.stl|thumb|3D model of a great inverted snub icosidodecahedron]]
In [[geometry]], the '''great inverted snub icosidodecahedron''' (or '''great vertisnub icosidodecahedron''') is a [[uniform star polyhedron]], indexed as U<sub>69</sub>. It is given a [[Schläfli symbol]] {{math|sr{{mset|{{Frac|5|3}},3}},}} and [[Coxeter-Dynkin diagram]] {{CDD|node_h|5|rat|d3|node_h|3|node_h}}. In the book ''[[Polyhedron Models]]'' by [[Magnus Wenninger]], the polyhedron is misnamed ''[[great snub icosidodecahedron]]'', and vice versa.

==Cartesian coordinates==

Let <math>\xi\approx -0.5055605785332548 </math> be the largest (least negative) negative zero of the polynomial <math>x^3+2x^2-\phi^{-2}</math>, where <math>\phi</math> is the [[golden ratio]]. Let the point <math>p</math> be given by
:<math>p=
\begin{pmatrix}
        \xi \\
        \phi^{-2}-\phi^{-2}\xi \\
        -\phi^{-3}+\phi^{-1}\xi+2\phi^{-1}\xi^2
\end{pmatrix}
</math>.
Let the matrix <math>M</math> be given by
:<math>M=
\begin{pmatrix}
         1/2  & -\phi/2 & 1/(2\phi) \\
         \phi/2   & 1/(2\phi)     & -1/2 \\
         1/(2\phi)     & 1/2  & \phi/2
\end{pmatrix}
</math>.
<math>M</math> is the rotation around the axis <math>(1, 0, \phi)</math>  by an angle of <math>2\pi/5</math>, counterclockwise. Let the linear transformations <math>T_0, \ldots, T_{11}</math> 
be the transformations which send a point <math>(x, y, z)</math> to the [[parity of a permutation|even permutations]] of <math>(\pm x, \pm y, \pm z)</math>  with an even number of minus signs. 
The transformations <math>T_i</math> constitute the group of rotational symmetries of a [[regular tetrahedron]].
The transformations <math>T_i M^j</math> <math>(i = 0,\ldots, 11</math>, <math>j = 0,\ldots, 4)</math> constitute the group of rotational symmetries of a [[regular icosahedron]].
Then the 60 points <math>T_i M^j p</math>  are the vertices of a great snub icosahedron. The edge length equals <math>-2\xi\sqrt{1-\xi}</math>, the circumradius equals <math>-\xi\sqrt{2-\xi}</math>, and the midradius equals <math>-\xi</math>.

For a great snub icosidodecahedron whose edge length is 1,
the circumradius is
:<math>R = \frac12\sqrt{\frac{2-\xi}{1-\xi}} \approx 0.6450202372957795 </math>
Its midradius is
:<math>r=\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{\frac{1}{1-\xi}} \approx 0.4074936889340787</math>

The four positive real roots of the [[sextic]] in {{math|''R''{{sup|2}}}},
<math display=block>4096R^{12} - 27648R^{10} + 47104R^8 - 35776R^6 + 13872R^4 - 2696R^2 + 209 = 0</math>
are the circumradii of the [[snub dodecahedron]] (U<sub>29</sub>), [[great snub icosidodecahedron]] (U<sub>57</sub>), great inverted snub icosidodecahedron (U<sub>69</sub>), and [[great retrosnub icosidodecahedron]] (U<sub>74</sub>).
{{-}}

== Related polyhedra ==

=== Great inverted pentagonal hexecontahedron ===
{{Uniform polyhedra db|Uniform dual polyhedron stat table|Gisid}}
[[File:Great inverted pentagonal hexecontahedron.stl|thumb|3D model of a great inverted pentagonal hexecontahedron]]
The '''great inverted pentagonal hexecontahedron''' (or '''petaloidal trisicosahedron''') is a nonconvex [[Isohedral figure|isohedral]] [[polyhedron]]. It is composed of 60 [[Concave polygon|concave]] pentagonal faces, 150 edges and 92 vertices.

It is the [[Dual polyhedron|dual]] of the [[uniform star polyhedron|uniform]] great inverted snub icosidodecahedron.
{{-}}

==Proportions==

Denote the [[golden ratio]] by <math>\phi</math>. Let <math>\xi\approx 0.252\,780\,289\,27</math> be the smallest positive  zero of the polynomial <math>P = 8x^3-8x^2+\phi^{-2}</math>. Then each pentagonal face has four equal angles of <math>\arccos(\xi)\approx 75.357\,903\,417\,42^{\circ}</math> and one angle of <math>360^{\circ}-\arccos(-\phi^{-1}+\phi^{-2}\xi)\approx 238.568\,386\,330\,33^{\circ}</math>. Each face has three long and two short edges. The ratio <math>l</math> between the lengths of the long and the short edges is given by
:<math>l = \frac{2-4\xi^2}{1-2\xi}\approx 3.528\,053\,034\,81</math>. 
The [[dihedral angle]] equals <math>\arccos(\xi/(\xi+1))\approx 78.359\,199\,060\,62^{\circ}</math>. Part of each face lies inside the solid, hence is invisible in solid models. The other two zeroes of the polynomial <math>P</math> play a similar role in the description of the [[great pentagonal hexecontahedron]] and the [[great pentagrammic hexecontahedron]].
